summary: Mara lands at Ossary on the third day of the storm and finds the Cold Lamp dark three nights; not one boat on the quay will cross to it.

states.c1: ashore at Ossary, refused a crossing by every boat in the harbour
states.c3: keeping clear of the crossing, offering her the weather instead of help

summary: The keepers' roll shows her brother struck out on the eleventh with another name written over his in newer ink; Halloran will not say that name aloud.

states.c1: has read the struck roll and holds a name that means nothing to her
states.c3: refuses to name the relief, on the quay or off it

summary: Ester Quill, warden of Gannet Isle, rules the brother drowned under article nine and offers Mara a paid passage home plus money for asking nothing further.

states.c1: told her brother is drowned; offered passage home and a price for silence
states.c4: has closed the matter under article nine and is buying quiet

summary: Halloran shows Mara the note of hand the warden holds over his boat and agrees to cross at the four o'clock slack for thirty-one.

states.c1: has bought a crossing for the four o'clock slack
states.c3: has taken her money and will cross east against the warden's request

summary: Mara and Halloran cross the Weathering on the four o'clock slack; the hour runs out, the channel turns over white behind them, and there is no slack back until four tomorrow.

states.c1: over the deep ground and committed; cannot return for a day
states.c3: has made the crossing and is keeping the boat off the landing

summary: They land on Calder Rock after dark; the tower door is unbarred and a wet track leads in and up, in prints smaller than Mara's own.

states.c1: inside the tower, a hundred and nine steps up, following a wet track

summary: Mara searches the tower room by room and finds it walked out of rather than emptied by force; the lens is wiped and squared, the reservoir is dry to the brass, and the lamp is cold.

states.c1: knows the lamp was put out deliberately, not failed

summary: The keeper's log shows three strokes rung on Gannet on the third and her brother still writing in it until the eleventh: a death bell eight days early.

states.c1: certain her brother was not drowned on the day the bell said
states.c3: come up the tower and looking at an empty lantern room

summary: Ester Quill, warden of Gannet Isle, rules the brother drowned under article nine after three days of unanswered bells and offers Mara a paid passage home plus money for asking nothing further.

states.c1: told her brother is drowned; offered passage home and a price for silence
states.c4: has closed the matter under article nine and is buying quiet

summary: The keeper's log shows three strokes rung on Gannet on the first and her brother's hand still writing until the ninth: a death bell eight days early.

states.c1: certain her brother was not drowned on the day the bell said
states.c3: come up the tower and looking at an empty lantern room

summary: Dov Ashe inventories the Calder store under article four while Mara lies hidden on the stair; the book says thirty casks and the floor holds nineteen.

states.c1: hidden on the iron stair, and now knows eleven casks are missing
states.c5: taking the inventory under orders and unsettled by his own count

summary: On Gannet, Nell Carrow tells Mara her brother is alive and put the Cold Lamp out himself, and asks whose side she will stand on when she finds him.

states.c1: knows her brother is alive and that he darkened the light himself
states.c6: has admitted going out to the Rock on the seventh and being turned back at the service room

summary: The eleven marked casks are in the island's salvage yard, entered as wreck goods under article four on the fifth - three days before the lamp went dark.

states.c1: holds a dated entry that puts the oil in the yard before there was any wreck
states.c6: has seen the date and is no longer able to treat it as rumour

summary: Quill catches Mara at the barrel head, confirms her brother is alive, and offers a Friday berth and a clean entry on the roll for her silence; Mara tears the page out and runs.

states.c1: has refused the warden's offer and is running with the torn ledger page
states.c4: has been refused for the first time and knows the date is out of her yard

summary: Dov Ashe runs Mara down on the flats and tells her the warden rang the death bell herself on the first, that his own name is the one over her brother's on the roll, and that her brother is on the Drowned Stair with the tide making; he lends her the punt.

states.c1: knows who rang the bell and where her brother is
states.c5: has broken with the warden: 'when she asks me I will have counted wrong'

summary: Mara crosses at half flood and finds Tem alive on the second step of the Drowned Stair with the mechanism crated and the lens lashed under the third step.

states.c1: on the Stair with her brother and a rising tide
states.c2: found, still hidden behind the explanation he has been rehearsing for four days

summary: Tem gives his account - a written direction to show the false character of the Sound light, one vessel lost, two more since he darkened the Rock - and refuses the punt without the mechanism; then the Calder bell rings twice for a wreck.

states.c1: has the whole account and a wreck sounding two miles off
states.c2: refusing to leave the mechanism; owns the three men by number

summary: Mara goes off the second step into forty feet of green water, cuts the lashing at the ringbolt and brings the lens up; when she surfaces the wreck bell has stopped.

states.c1: resolute: has gone down into the deep water and come back up with the lens
states.c2: holding her elbows on the step, the crate still with him

summary: Halloran had rung the wreck bell and stood by a ketch for two hours; he crosses the Weathering with Mara on the four o'clock slack, tells her plainly what the note of hand was really for, pays it off out of the salvage line, and the clerk takes the claim but wants the keeper's own hand before the fourteenth is out.

states.c1: has lodged the claim and needs her brother's signature inside a day
states.c3: free of the note, papers back in his own hand, and telling it straight

summary: Tem signs the claim in the watch room, knowing it names him keeper on the days he stripped the light, and undertakes to give the whole account to the roll; then asks who will light the lamp, because it will not be him.

states.c1: has the signed claim
states.c2: accountable: signed, and giving the article eleven direction and what followed it to the roll

summary: The claim goes in with two hours of the fourteenth left, the eleven casks come back, and Nell rebuilds the light, fills the reservoir and takes the keeper's oath she has refused for nine years; the first sweep catches an unlit lugger in the channel.

states.c1: on the Rock for the relighting
states.c6: sworn keeper of the Cold Lamp, showing three flashes to the minute

summary: Quill is taken off the lugger under article four, because a claim allowed inside the nine days took the eleven casks out of her wreck goods; Mara takes the relief watch and stands it facing the deep water.

states.c1: relief keeper on Calder Rock, standing the watch over the deepest ground in the archipelago
states.c4: exposed - held under her own article, with article eleven to follow
